latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Replication of dengue virus in dendritic cells, monocytes, macrophages, endothelial-adjacent cells, hepatocytes, and marrow stromal compartments. This mechanism is the early driver of fever, NS1 positivity, PCR positivity, leukopenia, and later immune amplification.

Interferon, IL-6, TNF, chemokines, complement, and monocyte activation producing high fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, rash, malaise, nausea, and modest inflammatory physiology.
Transient marrow suppression, leukocyte apoptosis, and monocyte/dendritic-cell infection causing leukopenia, neutropenia or relative lymphocytosis, and a viral blood picture during early illness.

Thrombocytopenia from marrow suppression, peripheral immune-mediated destruction, platelet activation, endothelial adhesion, and consumption at injured microvasculature. It is central to petechiae, mucosal bleeding, and procedural bleeding risk.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: NS1-complement endothelial glycocalyx injury and plasma leak
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: NS1, complement activation, mast-cell mediators, cross-reactive antibodies, and cytokines disrupt endothelial glycocalyx and tight junctions, producing transient capillary leak, hemoconcentration, pleural effusion, ascites, gallbladder edema, pulmonary edema, and shock during the critical phase.

Direct viral hepatocyte/Kupffer-cell injury, immune-mediated hepatitis, and hypoperfusion injury causing AST-predominant transaminitis, hepatomegaly, right upper quadrant pain, hyperbilirubinemia, hypoalbuminemia, coagulopathy, and rare acute liver failure.

Thrombocytopenia, platelet dysfunction, endothelial injury, intrinsic pathway abnormalities, liver synthetic dysfunction, and consumptive coagulopathy combine to create petechiae, mucosal bleeding, gastrointestinal bleeding, pulmonary hemorrhage, and intracranial hemorrhage in severe disease.

Intravascular depletion from capillary leak, vomiting, poor intake, myocardial depression, and bleeding reduces preload and tissue perfusion, driving tachycardia, hypotension, lactic acidosis, AKI, ARDS, hepatic ischemia, and mortality.

Direct viral or immune-mediated myocardial injury producing sinus tachycardia out of proportion to fever, T-wave changes, reduced ejection fraction, conduction block, cardiogenic component of shock, and pulmonary edema vulnerability.
Rare severe immune dysregulation with macrophage activation, very high ferritin, persistent cytopenias, hepatitis, pancreatitis, pneumonitis, HLH physiology, and high mortality if unrecognized.

axes.clinical_interpretation: Acute dengue should require dengue-specific virology/IgM support or a credible dengue epidemiologic source context. Prior dengue IgG alone, generic endemic/travel context, fever, rash, thrombocytopenia, bleeding, hemoconcentration, hepatitis, shock, or capillary leak alone should not unlock the manifold.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Lower platelets increase petechiae and purpura.
Very low platelets contribute to major bleeding risk.
INR prolongation from liver failure/coagulopathy increases bleeding risk.
Plasma leak raises hematocrit unless bleeding or hemodilution dominates.
Third spacing can rapidly deplete intravascular volume.
Effusions and pulmonary edema can impair oxygenation.
ARDS and pulmonary edema raise oxygen and ventilatory support needs.
Severe hepatic injury can progress to coagulopathy.
Acute liver failure materially increases mortality hazard.
Severe coagulopathy/bleeding can include intracranial hemorrhage.
Intracranial hemorrhage is a high-lethality bleeding complication.
Very high ferritin in dengue should raise HLH/macrophage-activation hazard.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Persistent vomiting or altered sensorium makes oral hydration unreliable.
Rising hematocrit, effusions, or shock physiology requires monitored IV fluid strategy.

treatments.context_specific_role: Stable dengue with reliable intake and no evolving critical-phase warning physiology.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Intravascular volume replacement is most useful when plasma leak is causing low effective circulating volume.
Once pulmonary edema or large effusions dominate, additional crystalloid can worsen oxygenation.
Myocardial dysfunction narrows safe fluid margin.

side_effects.interpretation: Excess fluid during plasma leak or myocarditis can worsen pulmonary edema.

treatments.context_specific_role: Main hemodynamic intervention in monitored critical-phase dengue; dose and duration depend on serial vitals, hematocrit, urine output, and respiratory status.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Myocardial dysfunction may require inotropic support rather than more fluid alone.

treatments.context_specific_role: Maintains perfusion when shock persists despite careful volume or when cardiac dysfunction/fluid overload makes additional crystalloid unsafe.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Acetaminophen exposure should be minimized or avoided when severe hepatic injury is evolving.

treatments.context_specific_role: Symptom and physiologic stress reduction while avoiding platelet-inhibiting or nephrotoxic antipyretics.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Platelets are most useful for active bleeding or invasive procedures, not isolated low counts.

treatments.context_specific_role: Active bleeding, invasive procedures, or extreme thrombocytopenia with compelling risk context.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Red cells restore oxygen delivery during major bleeding or severe anemia.

side_effects.interpretation: Blood product volume can worsen fluid overload in leak phase.

treatments.context_specific_role: Restores oxygen-carrying capacity when dengue bleeding or hemolysis produces clinically significant anemia.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Plasma or cryoprecipitate is directed to bleeding coagulopathy or procedures, not isolated mild lab prolongation.

side_effects.interpretation: Plasma volume can worsen pulmonary edema or leak-phase overload.

treatments.context_specific_role: Bleeding or procedure-directed correction of dengue coagulopathy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Advanced respiratory support requires equipment and trained staff.

treatments.context_specific_role: Oxygen, ventilatory support, and conservative fluid strategy for pulmonary edema, pleural effusions, ARDS, or pulmonary hemorrhage.
Supports severe AKI, hyperkalemia, acidosis, uremia, or fluid overload while dengue critical physiology resolves.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: NAC is most relevant when dengue hepatitis has progressed toward acute liver failure physiology.

treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunctive support in dengue-associated acute liver failure, especially while transplant or recovery trajectory is assessed.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: TPE requires specialized access, product, and monitoring.
Coagulopathy and vascular access can increase bleeding risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rescue consideration in severe dengue acute liver failure with hyperferritinemia or HLH-like immune activation.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Transplant depends on system feasibility and whether dengue recovery is likely without grafting.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rare pathway when dengue-associated acute liver failure continues to deteriorate despite supportive care.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Steroids, IVIG, or HLH-directed immunomodulation is not ordinary dengue shock treatment; it is a separate HLH-context intervention.
Concurrent bacterial infection can make immunosuppression hazardous.

side_effects.interpretation: Immunomodulation can worsen secondary infection risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Specialist-directed treatment for dengue-triggered HLH/macrophage activation after evidence supports that event chain.

supportive_care: Use serial assessment rather than a single lab value: vitals, pulse pressure, capillary refill, urine output, mental status, respiratory work, hematocrit, platelet count, AST/ALT, INR, creatinine, and lactate.
Do not treat isolated thrombocytopenia as the main disease target; interpret platelet trend with bleeding, hematocrit, leak signs, and procedure need.
During the critical phase, titrate isotonic fluid to effective circulating volume and stop or slow promptly when perfusion improves or respiratory/leak overload appears.
Avoid NSAIDs, aspirin, intramuscular injections, unnecessary central lines, and nonessential anticoagulation when bleeding risk is high.
Use ultrasound or CT evidence of pleural effusion, ascites, gallbladder wall edema, pericholecystic fluid, or periportal edema as plasma-leak evidence, not as separate disease labels.

Escalate to monitored or ICU care for shock, rising hematocrit with falling platelets, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, altered mental status, bleeding, hypoxemia, severe hepatitis, or AKI.
For acute liver failure, monitor glucose, INR, lactate, pH, ammonia when available, mental status, and intracranial bleeding risk; involve hepatology and critical care early.
For AKI or severe acidosis, involve nephrology early; balance dialysis vascular access against platelet and coagulopathy status.
For suspected myocarditis, obtain ECG, troponin when available, echocardiography, and continuous rhythm monitoring; avoid assuming all shock is fluid-responsive.

If fever persists beyond the expected dengue course, WBC becomes neutrophilic, or vascular access/invasive procedures occurred, actively evaluate secondary bacterial infection rather than attributing all fever to dengue.
Public-health actions include mosquito bite prevention, local reporting where required, and household/outbreak exposure review.
distillation_quality_notes: Disease-name scope is pure: Disease: Dengue, id D-DENGUE. Severe dengue, hemorrhagic fever, shock, serotype, travel region, secondary infection, and HLH are represented as mechanisms, axes, risks, events, or treatment context.
No semantic treatment ranking labels are used; treatment roles are represented as vector-field, push-state, or modifier structure.
